Name: Sara Stone
Question: Are Ouija boards really dangerous in a way that a demonic entity can be let in?
Old_Answer: Yes. The imagination is one of the most important, potent, creative faculties at mankind’s disposal. The use of speculation, when it comes to matters involving the future, whether it is in “sports” like gambling on the horses or the slot machine, or using a “magic” board to let you in on secrets makes the human mind search for the unknown and to some extent unknowable (except through God) IN the unknown… It’s like going to a ballot box and voting on Door Number 1 without knowing what is behind door number 1. This kind of non-thinking, yet pining for some sort of “significant” or meaningful result raises the fear or anxiety level in a person, which also makes one prone to grasp any straw that volunteers itself. If the good can come through this way (and it doesn’t, for the good is not imprecise nor wishy washy nor speculative per se), then so can the bad. Therefore, stay away from these things. It is your desire to have something for free (as opposed to seeking counsel from God with whom you are in a relationship) that allows the dark side to bind you. You are volunteering for the bondage. Why go slave when you can be a free man?
Answer_with_writing_sample: Thank you for this intriguing question about Ouija boards and their potential dangers. I appreciate the opportunity to share my thoughts on this topic. To begin with, I believe that the perception of Ouija boards as a gateway for demonic entities is largely influenced by cultural narratives and personal experiences rather than empirical evidence. Many people approach these boards with a sense of curiosity, but it’s crucial to recognize that the energy and intention behind the use of the board play significant roles in the outcomes. If someone approaches a Ouija board with fear or negativity, they may inadvertently invite unsettling experiences. This is not to say that there aren't accounts of strange occurrences associated with Ouija boards; however, these can often be attributed to psychological factors, such as the ideomotor effect, where individuals subconsciously move the planchette without realizing it. It’s also essential to consider the mindset of the participants—if they are open to the idea of communicating with spirits, they may interpret ambiguous experiences as supernatural. In my view, the real danger lies not in the board itself but in the mindset and emotional state of those using it. Therefore, if one chooses to engage with a Ouija board, it’s wise to do so with a grounded perspective, clear intentions, and an understanding of the psychological dynamics at play. Ultimately, whether or not one believes in the supernatural, maintaining a healthy skepticism and self-awareness is key to navigating such experiences safely.
Answer_with_user_profile:

However, the fear surrounding them largely stems from their portrayal in popular media and folklore, which tends to sensationalize the idea of summoning spirits. Engaging with a Ouija board should be done with caution and respect, but labeling it as inherently dangerous may overlook the personal and subjective nature of these experiences. Ultimately, whether or not one believes in the potential for demonic influence, the most significant factor is the mindset and intentions of those involved. If approached with an open mind and a sense of responsibility, the experience can be more about exploration than danger.

Name: Sara Stone
Question: What is the one thing you feel you need to have to be truly content with your life, and what all would you sacrifice to get it?
Old_Answer: Number one thing: Reparations to all I have done wrong to or harmed, financially or otherwise. Especially, to my son, now an adult, whom I wronged through mistreatment. What all would I sacrifice to get it? First, my limited mindset about how best to produce financially has to go. Heretofore, I have operated out of only one framework: Start at the bottom, work hard, and rely on others to advance you. I need a better strategy. Presently, my son (and roommate) brings in more income than I; he is putting more money out for our overhead. It is reasonable, therefore, to be experiencing pressure to do better, both from within, and from without. Old habits die hard. They must be replaced by new ones with more payoffs. The biggest temptation is to hurry up and end the pain of cognitive dissonance, to get back up on that horse again, to once again join the majority of America’s lower-wage earners in a job with no benefits, where you don’t even know your schedule or number of hours from week to week, let alone are enabled to participate in a health insurance network that is worth your heard earned dough. But at least I’d be “doing my best,” right? “Doing right,” by “carrying my fair share,” isn’t that right? WRONG. All I would be doing is all that I have ever done before and it has NEVER worked. It ISN’T realistic that such an approach would ever work; it is an approach that has only functioned to bind me, to keep me down. You sit there in those positions, doing your best, all the while stilling your anger and discontent and reality-based worry about your future, thinking, “I’m doing the right thing;” Consoling yourself, “What else can be done?” Repeating mantras like, “It isn’t all my fault, that’s just the way things are.” Or worst of all, “Don’t worry, it’ll all be over soon.” I cannot and will not do that crap ever again in my life, period. So…. NEW STORY!! I’m flying off, like a straight-edged tangent, bouncing off that circle of enclosure over options that will never open to a different reality, earnestly applying myself instead to simple things, in order to change what has been the status quo in my life for years. I am shutting down what has been my modus operandi and risking being exposed for a phony, an ignoramus, an under-achiever who’s actually just stupid, or dumb, or whatever I think I might “really” be. Simple things first: I am treating my son with more kindness; finding ways to negotiate and stand up for myself with less scream and more “you and me,” not just me; focusing on progress and insisting I make some; making sure there’s something in it for him. In so doing, I am protecting that part of me that conceives; the heart/spirit/brain-womb in me, that captures reality potential floating through the air, that cannot lite upon the dry hard pan ground of sheer drudgery. Instead, I am refusing to off that fertile body’s offspring before it gets a chance to grow. I am protecting it, and in so doing, I am protecting me. Interestingly enough, it seems that baby ideas, like little babies in the human womb, only survive in safety, with something to hang onto. It’s not enough that an idea is good. Or, perhaps in respect of one of America’s biggest over achievers, Jeff Bezos, I can agree that inspiration is 1%, 99% of success is in execution. The support of branches, of a sturdy vine, a labyrinth of options to shelter that baby from what would strike it down, is what comes next. Therefore, besides setting aside many personal patterns related to having a work life that’s DOA, another sacrifice I must make is to let go of control in the establishing of and maintenance of relational connection with others. For the ideas I wish to incubate are nearly all related on one level or another to community building; I like seeing other people pick up the power cords to their own abilities and plug them in. Most of my ideas are related to improving the chances of that happening for individuals by establishing frameworks for community interaction that highlight both needs and opportunities - where the exposures of both of these sides of the coin of life exponentially increases the number of ways in which individuals can exert their own opinions and utilize their usually under-utilized skills, talents and abilities for the common good. I believe we human beings were made to function together like this. So, I am letting myself out of the prison yard of compulsion and death, and moving into the wilds of personal interactions with mindfulness of mutual respect and keeping an open mind, because you never know what you have that someone else needs, or what they have that you might need, or, in the case at hand, that your idea might need. My desire is to meet my goal of furnishing my son and others with full reparations by using my abilities to perceive and conceive, to let people see how amazing God is and what good ideas He has by setting aside all my junk and let HIM birth good stuff out of me. Thank you for asking to answer this, Mr. Deer. I hope it is helpful to some one out there.

This connection is not just about being physically present with people; it’s about sharing experiences, supporting one another, and fostering a sense of belonging. In a world that often feels isolating, the warmth of genuine relationships can be a balm for the soul. I would sacrifice a lot to cultivate and maintain these connections. For instance, I would willingly give up certain luxuries, like dining out frequently or indulging in expensive hobbies, if it meant I could invest more time and energy into nurturing my relationships. I would also prioritize my time, choosing to spend less on distractions like excessive screen time or social media, which can create a false sense of connection but often leave me feeling more alone. Instead, I would focus on meaningful interactions—whether it’s a heartfelt conversation over coffee, a weekend getaway with loved ones, or simply being present for someone in need. The richness of life is found in these moments of shared laughter, tears, and support. Ultimately, I believe that the sacrifices I make in pursuit of these connections will yield a far greater return in terms of happiness and fulfillment than any material possession ever could. Life is fleeting, and the bonds we create are what truly matter; they are the threads that weave the fabric of a contented existence.

Question: How does Benny Hinn get people to fall down and act like they do once they are on the ground?
Old_Answer: I thought it was phony. I had a then-older friend who had a mess of a house, a terrible childhood, widowhood from a man whom she might have been surely better off without as he used to beat her and their son, and she LOVED Benny Hinn. She was also a VERY powerful “prayer” warrior. Phenomenal at prophecy, though extremely humble and nearly non-existent ego. When I would stop by or call and hear Benny Hinn in the background, I said nothing, but I would just think, perhaps as you or MANY others do, “Well, if that comforts her, more power to her!” WOW, was I arrogant. I had NO idea this stuff was real. I mean NONE. Makes sense though, doesn’t it? For some of us who jump to conclusions that because our experience hasn’t been a certain way, a certain experience must be manufactured, false, or made up? I think so. Well, after my friend died, my son and I were invited to visit a Friday night meeting with a lady “prophet” who “walked in healing” and so on, (those quotes mean she has the spiritual gift(s) of healing and prophecy). People were going up and “getting slain by the spirit.” I thought, okay, what the heck… when my son asked if he should go up. I said sure, if you want. My son has some very special gifts anyway, and I had learned to trust his judgment on certain things, but I sure as heck didn’t need it. He went up, the lady put her hand on his chest, without any force really, then looked up at him when he didn’t “go down.” She stepped back and thought, or prayed, or both, and then put her hand on him again, with a little more force, and WHOMP, he went down and stayed down. Now, skeptics may feel, or conclude, this is hocus pocus, she pushed him down. Nah, my kid was 6′2″ and 170 pounds then and I can guarantee he wasn’t “pushed” down… But, you say, auto-suggestion… Nah, my son IS gullible in some ways… but NOT in this manner. He takes spiritual stuff seriously. He knows it’s not a game and he doesn’t take anyone else’s word, including his mother’s, for anything. Stubborn “young” fool that he is. Anyway, truly, he sorts it all out himself. Well, he went down and stayed down for a bit; when he came back to the chair next to me, he just felt to me to be a bit more relaxed. Okay, REALLY relaxed. But he didn’t say much to me about it until much much later, a couple YEARS later. We went to visit Charis Bible College here in Colorado Springs, Colorado, one Sunday for a special healing service where they had arranged to bring in a world renown “healer.” He had called on the Wednesday prior to let them know he couldn’t make it…. he was worn out and needed rest, and so he cancelled What were Pastor Lawson Purdue and Andrew Wommack to do? Well, they decided to go ahead and have the event, and they put themselves wholly into the event. My son and I were sitting in the back. There was a long time period after a lesson of sorts, of people of all ages sizes and shapes ministering to those who asked for healing all around the large auditorium off of Elkton (this is before their move up to Woodland Park). A minister of Lawson’s came up to me when I was interceding while others were praying for a woman wheelchair-bound with multiple sclerosis. “Ma’am, Do you need healing?” “Oh, no, I’m fine, I’M PRAYING FOR OTHERS,” I proudly announced, because you see, NO ONE’S GONNA fool around with MY BODY, MY HEALING, MY SPIRITUAL LIFE…. I’m no fool!!!! Oh, but what a fool I was, my intellect pierced through with pride. Fortunately for me, the band of do-gooders around this one woman in the wheelchair dissolved, and all of a sudden, I find myself faced with this Texan in a 10-gallon hat, saying, loudly, “MA’AM, may I pray for your?” And barely before I could get a syllable out, this guy has his hand on my neck, and I start feeling this INCREDIBLE feeling, this warmth, like I have never felt before in my life, or since. AND THEN this thing started happening… It was like a humongous, hot flapping butterfly was on top of my head, flapping his wings up and down, up and down, but I wasn’t letting go. I looked around, I weigh a good deal, and I thought, I am not going down with catchers around me… there seemed to be none; the phenomenon continued, all of a sudden, my son was behind me with another man, THEN I remembered what my son had finally told me one day about his experience with that lady, “I just knew, Mom, that if I let go it would feel really, really, good.” I let go. BAM… I went down into those men’s arms and laid on that floor for a bit. I had never had anything like this happen to me, though I was filled with the Holy Ghost when I had a priest in the Episcopal Church lay his apostolic bishopy hand on my head for confirmation in sixth grade… (I began to speak in tongues afterwards but did not know what that was). But, the most amazing thing about this experience, is that it didn’t end. For TWO WEEKS solid, I was in another world. It was like, and believe, me, I had never ever ever put these silly sounding words together in the same sentence before, and no, no one told me this is what you say, or what not, but it was like a few drops of “golden anointing oil,” had been spread throughout my whole being. It was one of the loveliest experiences I have ever had in my life. So, that’s MY experience. But it wasn’t about Benny Hinn. This one is: Todd White was meeting a drug dealer. Addicted to porn by age 10, drugs by 12, this then teen-ager, had conceived the brilliant plan (a way to get yourself shot, actually) to cheat a drug dealer by pretending he was an undercover cop and demanding on the goods…. When the shots started to ring out from the dealer’s 9mm, White was standing next to his car and only about 10 to 12 feet I think it was from the gun. The bullets did not hit him; It was as though they went THROUGH HIM into other objects around him. He got in his car and sped off in total shock and freaked out then heard a voice, “I took those bullets for you, Todd.” Great, Todd thought, now I’m f***ed with the dealer, gonna get killed, AND I’m losing my mind. But there is was again. And then he told Todd he was Jesus. Which freaked him out ever more. So, without going into more detail, Todd was saved that night, and began growing in the Lord right away, but was not getting the results he wanted. He wanted his laying of hands on people to work, just the way the bible says. He wanted to see the blind see and the deaf hear and lame walk. So, he decided to try some Christian conferences. At one, he decided to sit up front. All of a sudden, the speaker pointed at him and told him to come up front. Todd was surprised, but went up. The man looked at Todd, who was several feet from him, with two very large men behind him to “catch” him or help if anything went down. All of a sudden, the man said something, made a move with his arm toward Todd, and TODD AND THE TWO CATCHERS went up in the air four feet and BACK six feet as they heard what sounded like crackling in the air… something like thunder. Todd was stunned, the catchers were caught off guard. And as Todd came around, and sat up and then stood up, he stood in front of the man once more, and said, “AGAIN.” BOOM, up four feet (with the other two BIG guys, again) and back six. Todd was discombobulated. Could not speak. Was receiving power from on high and did not know his name hardly. The two ushers gathered their wits, readied themselves to carry Todd off the stage, then the man of God said to the Man of God, “I NEED MORE OF JESUS;” and ONE MORE TIME. So, do I know someone who was healed “by faith?” Does that mean “faith healing…” like someone laid hands on them and they got well? I can tell you this. I have met two people who “had” multiple sclerosis and in the case of one, then in her 70’s when I met her, she had been free from MS symptoms ever since she had, what she experienced as a healing from God… no big event, just as a “result” of her faith in God and she believed God healed her, more than 20 years prior. He explained that this learning process as it applied to his body and disease, took “seven years to learn to walk in the healing that Jesus died for us to have access to…” So, as Elery put it, “Now, if they x-rayed my grey matter, they might still find those plaques… they were still there the last time I got those pictures… “ but the last time was more than a decade ago… “but fact is, the only time I get symptoms is if someone comes up who is trying to get healed from MS.” My own personal introduction to what I might call the physics of faith (though I am not talking just in terms of what might be some of the thinking in “Christian Science”) was through Elery… he taught the SUPRA-natural world behind this one… and gradually I have gotten more and more into the Spirit. The most successful scenarios depend on the asker’s character and record of production within the community they are going to for help. If, for instance, you are a fantastic volunteer at your church, and have been tithing and an active member for several years, IF the church doesn’t have a policy against it, this person may find their need quickly met. I recall my father, a 13-year old when the Depression hit the USA in 1932, telling about the “only” time he ever borrowed money from someone other going to a bank for establishing a mortgage on a piece of real estate. It was 1945; he had been back from the war for two years, had two children as well as two step children off and on, and had been working for Alexander Film Company as a pilot and then in sales. He had earned a Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration from the Colorado College before he signed up for the Air Corps, so he knew well the value of a dollar SAVED, and that renting was a losing proposition. A small house on Harrison Street came up for sale just a few blocks from the film company’s buildings on North Nevada Avenue, and it had a good price. He approached a man he worked with who was familiar with his work ethic and abilities, and indeed secured a personal loan of $3,000 to put down on what would become his home. By then immediately dividing the place in to an upstairs-downstairs duplex, and securing a solid couple to rent from him, he was able to pay that man back in short order, securing another step in establishing a good reputation which continued to build and be stable over a lifetime of living. If, Tim, you asked this due to the number of needs that may be arising out of COVID-19 based unemployment or paychecks missing in action, I think the best approach is to have a plan of how the need is not going to be reoccurring, because one thing many helpers do not want to do is “throw money down the drain.” Therefore, having a plan of how one will not need this money in the future, and explaining your creative ways and past ways of meeting such difficulties and overcoming them should help.
